subject: HelioHealth dedicated pool provisioning — initial scope and next steps
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@heliohealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool for HelioHealth — sizing and regional preference

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood Dedicated yesterday. We discussed reserved capacity for our inference pipelines and wanted to start scoping the initial provisioning. High level:
- Production inference for clinical triage (p95 latency target 150ms) across US east and US west.
- Expected steady throughput: ~12 reqs/sec (avg 100 tokens), spiking to 60 reqs/sec during morning batch processing windows.
- Data residency: US only; SOC 2 evidence required.

Can you share the next steps for the pool sizing exercise and what you need from our side (network contacts, peak traces, expected sequence lengths)? Also curious how Redwood handles cross-region burst (we may want warm capacity in the other region).

Sara
Sara Patel
Head of ML Ops — HelioHealth
--
HelioHealth | sara@heliohealth.com
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool for HelioHealth — sizing and regional preference

Hi Sara — great to get this started. Short answers and next steps:

1) What we need from you:
   - 72h representative trace/export of request rates + token length distribution (CSV or JSON).
   - Network allowlist (egress IP ranges) and a NetOps contact for peering.
   - SOC2 point of contact and any acceptance criteria for audit evidence.

2) Cross-region burst model: Redwood supports warm standby in a second region and automatic cross-region failover. You can configure an active primary (us-east) and an async warm pool in us-west with automatic burst-scaling up to a configured cap. We recommend a warm capacity sized to 30–50% of peak to reduce cold-starts.

3) Sizing: we’ll run a quick simulation after we ingest your 72h traces. That will propose pool topology (number of GPUs, machine types), expected p95 latency, and a recommended autoscale/burst policy.

Action: I’ll put together a short intake checklist and a kickoff agenda. Can we schedule a 30m ops handoff tomorrow at 10am PT with your NetOps?

Thanks — Logan
Logan Wright
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool for HelioHealth — sizing and regional preference

Team — looping in ops/implementation planning. Ben, Grace: please review Sara's bullets and prep the simulation plan. Proposed checklist I’ll share with the customer:

- Intake items: 72h traces, NetOps contact + allowlist, SOC2 POC, desired SLA (99.9%?), expected cutover date window.
- Preflight: network tests, IAM & KMS scoping, model artifacts + quantization notes.
- Provision plan: initial pool (us-east primary), warm standby (us-west) with 40% warm-sizing, canary routing policy, A/B model rollout policy.
- Autoscale policy draft: baseline scale at 20% headroom over steady state, burst threshold at 85% utilization, max burst ceiling tied to reserved burst buffer.
- Runbook items: rollback to hosted model, throttle policy, on-call escalation.

I’ll draft the activation playbook and attach the topology diagram. Ben, can you include network egress ranges and expected kernel/runtime choices for a 7B quantized model?

Monica
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool for HelioHealth — sizing and regional preference

Monica — preliminary notes based on Sara's workload:

- Suggested baseline topology (provisional): 4x A10G-style instances in us-east for primary pool (continuous batching + KV prefix cache enabled). Warm standby: 2x similar machines in us-west.
- Kernel/runtime: prefer int8 quantized runtime for 7B family; will default to fused attention kernels and enable continuous batching with a 20ms max batch latency cap to hit p95 target.
- Autoscale/burst: baseline target = steady throughput + 20% headroom. Burst policy: allow autoscale up to 3x baseline for 30-minute sustained spikes; require manual approval for >3x for billing control.
- NetOps: egress IP ranges: 34.210.0.0/16, 52.15.128.0/18 (provisional) — will confirm exact list.

Attaching: pool-topology-diagram.png and a draft autoscale policy (autoscale-burst-policy-draft.xlsx). I’ll build the simulation once we have traces.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Patel <sara@heliohealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@heliohealth.com
Date: 2026-09-15T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool for HelioHealth — sizing and regional preference

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. We’ll: 
- Share the 72h traces (security team will scrub PII) by end of day Monday.
- Send NetOps contact (alex.netops@heliohealth.com) and confirm peering windows.
- SOC2 contact is rachel.audit@heliohealth.com.

We like the warm-standby approach with 40% sizing. Please include the canary routing and fallback policy in the playbook so our SREs can review. Also request that the activation playbook includes the exact verification steps you’ll run during canary (latency probe endpoints, error budgets, and traffic ramp cadence).

If that’s agreeable, we can lock the kickoff for Tuesday 10am PT to walk through the intake checklist and assign owners.

Sara
